correctness.rationale: The cited genus-degree formula gives \(g=1+Be/2\). Setting \(q=k+1\) and \(R_i=\binom{d_i+k}{k}\), the expected-dimension equation yields \(qB=\sum_i(d_i-1)R_i-(q^2+1)\). The proof then exhausts the three possibilities for the number of defining equations. For at least three equations the elementary lower bound is sharp only for three quadrics with \(q=2\); for two equations the all-quadric case violates the required divisibility and any larger degree is strictly above the threshold; for one equation the quadric case is excluded and the remaining lower bounds are strict. Thus \(B\ge2\) with the stated unique equality. The equality calibration \((e,g)=(128,129)\) is explicitly recorded in the source.

value.rationale: One-dimensional Fano schemes are classical geometric objects used in the study of complete intersections and intermediate Jacobians. The result converts a general formula into a sharp global restriction on their embedded geometry: genus always exceeds Pluecker degree, and the unique closest case is identified exactly. This rules out all low-genus possibilities in one statement and isolates the three-quadric line curve as the unique extremal object.
